title: Splice junctions and PSI
methods:
**Data.** The cohort's 10x datasets from FASTQs on their 2024-A references. Cells: barcodes STARsolo EmptyDrops_CR calls.

**Reference and competitor.** STARsolo is the only tool that counts junctions per cell with UMIs. It runs twice on the same reads: at STAR/STARsolo defaults (reference) and in the manual's Cell Ranger 4+ emulation (competitor). Singlet is compared with the reference; the Cell Ranger-emulation run is compared with the same reference. Singlet must be at least as close as that. The emulation's MultiGeneUMI_CR filter zeroes high-count junctions in overlapping genes, so it is not the natural reference for junctions.

**Filtered set.** STAR passes junctions through its outSJfilter* rules. A tool's filtered set is the junctions that pass them (STARsolo: its SJ feature list; Singlet: star_sj_pass in sj_features.tsv, from Singlet's own STAR alignment) and have at least one UMI in the STARsolo-called cells. Singlet also counts junctions outside that set; they are not scored.

**Metrics.** (1) Jaccard of the filtered sets. (2) Pearson r of log10(1 + UMI) summed over cells, over the union of the filtered sets. (3) Median over cells of the Pearson r of log1p junction UMI over junctions non-zero in either tool (reference junction list). (4) Pearson r across cells of the per-cell total junction UMI. (5) Cassette-exon PSI, pseudobulk, at least 20 UMI in every tool. (6) The same PSI per cell and event with at least 5 UMI. Cassette exons are annotated triples of consecutive exons (inclusion 1, inclusion 2, skipping) in the GTF; PSI = inclusion / (inclusion + skipping), inclusion = the mean of the two inclusion junctions.

**Rule.** match_or_beat the Cell Ranger-emulation run; tolerance = half-width of the paired bootstrap 95% CI of the difference (junctions, events or cells resampled together). All settings were fixed before the metrics were computed.

tools.name: singlet
tools.params: singlet encode --reads R1.fastq.gz R2.fastq.gz -o s.1fq; singlet s.1fq --ref-base $REF --genome-dir $REF/$SPECIES/star_2.7.11b --exons $REF/$SPECIES/genes/genes.gtf --out-prefix $OUT/ --threads 8 --pipeline --output-format mtx --raw-matrix  (sj_counts: molecules per junction and barcode; filtered set = star_sj_pass in sj_features.tsv)

tools.name: starsolo-sj
tools.params: STAR --runThreadN 16 --genomeDir $GENOME --readFilesIn $R2 $R1 --readFilesCommand zcat --soloType CB_UMI_Simple --soloCBwhitelist $WHITELIST --soloCBlen 16 --soloUMIstart 17 --soloUMIlen $UMILEN --soloBarcodeReadLength 0 --soloStrand $STRAND --soloFeatures SJ --outSAMtype None  (all other options at their defaults; $UMILEN 12 for v3, 10 for v2 and 5'; 10x v1: CB 14, UMI 10)

tools.name: starsolo-sj-cr
tools.params: STAR --runThreadN 16 --genomeDir $GENOME --readFilesIn $R2 $R1 --readFilesCommand zcat --soloType CB_UMI_Simple --soloCBwhitelist $WHITELIST --soloCBlen 16 --soloUMIstart 17 --soloUMIlen $UMILEN --soloBarcodeReadLength 0 --soloStrand $STRAND --soloFeatures Gene GeneFull Velocyto SJ --soloCellFilter EmptyDrops_CR --soloCBmatchWLtype 1MM_multi_Nbase_pseudocounts --soloUMIfiltering MultiGeneUMI_CR --soloUMIdedup 1MM_CR --clipAdapterType CellRanger4 --outFilterScoreMin 30 --outSAMtype None

caveats: There is only one junction-counting tool, STARsolo. Its default-settings run is the reference and its Cell Ranger-emulation run stands in for the competitor; the metrics say how close Singlet is to STARsolo relative to how far a second STARsolo configuration is, not how accurate either is against a biological truth.

The reference choice was made after looking at pbmc1k_v3: with the Cell Ranger emulation as reference, every Singlet metric scored below the default-settings run, because MultiGeneUMI_CR gives zero UMI to some of the highest-count junctions (overlapping genes). The default settings are STARsolo's documented defaults and were used for every dataset; the other orientation is not reported as a metric.
Singlet and STARsolo run separate STAR alignments (Singlet's inside its pipeline), so the junction sets differ in part through alignment settings, not only counting.
Singlet reports many more junctions than pass STAR's filters (most of them with a single molecule); those unfiltered junctions are excluded from every metric here.
Cassette-exon PSI uses annotated GENCODE triples only; novel exons and other event types (alternative donors and acceptors) are not scored. Singlet's own splice_psi output is not evaluated here.
Wall time and memory in resources are from a shared cluster at differing thread counts and are not a speed comparison.
Cohort datasets assigned to junctions-psi that this document does not cover (no run for them in this benchmark yet): pbmc5k_v4_d1, ding2020_pbmc1_smartseq2.
conclusion: On 7 datasets, Singlet's filtered junction set overlaps STARsolo SJ (at defaults) at Jaccard 0.84-0.96, its per-cell junction counts correlate at a median 0.42-0.94 and cassette-exon PSI at r = 0.972-0.999 (pseudobulk). Each is compared with STARsolo in Cell Ranger emulation measured against the same reference; 40 of 42 comparisons pass. Against the Cell Ranger emulation as reference Singlet agrees less (reported, not gated): that filter zeroes some high-count junctions.
